All 9 tests pass with this diff, but the implementation no longer matches the docstring it's supposed to be faithfully implementing, and the docstring was left unchanged.

Rule 2 of the docstring says a small word is lowercased "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`" — nothing about colons. But the new code adds a third, undocumented exception:

```python
is_after_colon = index > 0 and result[index - 1].endswith(":")
if is_first or is_last or is_after_colon:
    result.append(word.capitalize())
```

This `is_after_colon` branch exists solely to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass ("field: a year of remote work" → "Field: A Year of Remote Work"). Per the literal docstring, "a" here is neither the first nor last word of the whole string, so it should stay lowercase — but the code capitalizes it anyway. That's a rule invented to satisfy one specific test case, not something derivable from the current docstring text.

Since the teammate was explicit that "the docstrings are the source of truth" and asked not to touch the tests, this PR needed one of two things instead of silently adding new behavior:
1. Update the docstring to actually document the colon-triggered capitalization rule (so it reflects real behavior), or
2. Flag back to the teammate that `test_subtitle_after_colon` contradicts the documented spec, since as written the spec and the test disagree.

As submitted, the code and docstring are now inconsistent — a future reader trusting the docstring will misunderstand how colons affect output. Please reconcile the docstring with the actual (colon-aware) behavior, or raise the discrepancy instead of quietly coding around it.
